record.original_question: If G is a planar subcubic graph, must its HL-index R(G) always be at most 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 22 (Mohar [110]). If G is a planar subcubic graph, then R(G) ≤ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$ denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Define the two median eigenvalues of $G$ as $\lambda_H(G) = \lambda_{\lceil n/2 \rceil}(G)$ and $\lambda_L(G) = \lambda_{\lceil (n+1)/2 \rceil}(G)$, and define the HL-index of $G$ by
\[ R(G) = \max\bigl(|\lambda_H(G)|,\ |\lambda_L(G)|\bigr). \]
A graph is called subcubic if every vertex has degree at most $3$, and planar if it can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings.

Prove or disprove: for every planar subcubic graph $G$, one has $R(G) \le 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Mohar) appears to still be open in general. It is known that R(G) ≤ √2 for every subcubic graph (Mohar), with equality only for the Heawood graph, and recent work has verified Mohar's conjecture for K₄-minor-free subcubic graphs and other sparse subclasses, but the full planar case remains unresolved as of recent (2024–2025) papers.

status_evidence.snippet: R(G) = max{|λH|,|λL|}; Mohar's conjecture R(G) ≤ 1 for planar subcubic graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the HL-index and states the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Median eigenvalues of subcubic graphs (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on median eigenvalues of subcubic graphs continues to investigate Mohar's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues to investigate Mohar's conjecture, indicating it is not yet fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on median eigenvalues of subcubic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Mohar's Conjecture holds for every K4-minor-free subcubic graph.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for special subclasses but the planar case remains open.
